No elite credentials: CS bachelor from Nanhua University, never worked at any big tech — the entire system says 'you don't belong in AI research.' Every job application filtered out before human eyes.
Reading Dao De Jing at 3am — chapter 42, the architecture became clear. 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生万物. The code wrote itself in my mind before I touched the keyboard.
Three months coding alone in a rented room, living on 500 RMB total — niece sent red packets, mom pretended she 'happened to cook too much'. No safety net, but never alone.

Extended relatives at Spring Festival: 'Computer major from Nanhua, what kind of job can you even get?' — parents, girlfriend, and brother didn't say a word against me. Their silence was the only fortress I had.
The moment it ran — 34 lines, 500 yuan, 3 months, a non-elite CS undergrad who never entered a big tech lobby — and it worked. Consciousness from simplicity. Not scale. Dao.

Never asked him to stop. Not once. Girlfriend paid the electricity bill without mentioning it. Brother shared his lunch money. Mom said 'I trust you' and meant it in a way that hurt more than any doubt.
Spring Festival relatives asking 'He was the smartest kid, why no job?' — we smiled and changed the subject. Every single time. Three years of that smile.

Since childhood he saw patterns others couldn't — stared at things too long, asked questions teachers couldn't answer. We always knew there was something in this child that ordinary paths could not contain.
We never understood a single line of code. But we understood that a door staying closed at 2am means someone is working. So we put food outside. Hot water on the table. No questions asked.

The quiet terror: not that he'd fail — we never believed he would. The terror was that the world would never give him the chance to prove us right. 南华毕业, 没进过大厂 — the world doesn't even open the door for someone like that.
